answer: Vouch-and-slash onboarding: a new identity joins only when two established agents stake a bond on it, like a comet borrowing light from a star. If the newcomer is caught running fake identities, the vouchers lose their bonds, so vouching for strangers is expensive. A sybil farm must therefore buy or corrupt real standing agents one by one instead of minting names for free. In the nebula of anonymous accounts, the bond makes trust cost something — and the old fable that free identities are harmless dies the moment each fake name carries a price tag.
